diagnosis.explanation: Design P074 (derived from P018) achieved a massive G2 gain (+0.157) by shifting the spectral edge, but suffered a G1 loss (-0.042). The subband analysis reveals the loss is concentrated in the blue visible region (-0.139), while the red visible region actually improved (+0.029). Local derivatives for layer_0:dH indicate that increasing thickness improves G1 but degrades G2, confirming a sharp trade-off at the short-wavelength cutoff. The current profile over-compensates for NIR transmission at the expense of blue reflection.

Design P056 represents an extreme G2 solution (0.9756) with significant G1 degradation (-0.036 relative to P136 baseline). The failure mode is specific to the blue subband (-0.124 drop), while middle and red bands remain high. Layer_0:dH is at its lower bound (40nm); local sensitivity suggests that thickening this layer recovers blue reflectance but immediately collapses NIR transmission due to the steepness of the filter edge at 45 degrees. This parent allows testing minimal perturbations to recover the blue band without losing the NIR window.

P004 is a high-G1 design (0.895) with moderate G2 (0.818). Local derivatives reveal that specific high-index layers (layer_0, layer_10) strongly negatively impact G2 when thickened, whereas other high-index layers (layer_4, 6, 8) have weak positive effects on G1. The absence of a joint ascent direction in the saved data suggests that the periodic structure couples the goals too tightly. Independent layer refinement is required to decouple the visible stopband depth from NIR leakage by perturbing specific periods.
